checks: Positive scaling multiplies both the numerator and the support denominator by the same scalar and preserves the closed cap. Since D contains a neighborhood of the origin, h_D(u) is strictly positive for every nonzero continuous normal.

D_all is exactly the zero-base slice of C−C, so compactness, convexity and symmetry hold. A positive integer fiber contributes a neighborhood of zero to both bodies. The finite convex hull used for D_int is compact, and its generators lie in D_all.
Substituting z=U⁻¹(z′−k) and x=A⁻¹(x′−Bz−b) gives the stated transformed coefficients and in particular the plus signs in b′. Continuous normals stay nonzero.

Same-base translations and the shear cancel in the differences. Integral unimodularity preserves exactly the positive-volume integer index set, and the fiber Jacobian is |det A| independently of z. The transformed support denominator is unchanged, so both normalized ratios are invariant.
The original Opening (1) and §1 (2) give the same quotient, both distinct normalizing bodies, and the exact block-map formulas.

overlap.comparison: The accepted potential uses a fixed Euclidean unit continuous normal, and its existence and positivity statement does not assert covariance under a general invertible continuous block or track either intrinsic width body.

readability: The ratio is used for a nonempty positive-volume family, so M>0. When D_all is used, the sampled fibers are those of C.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The ratio and cap masses are invariant under the stated lattice-preserving block affine maps, and the two difference bodies transform by the continuous linear block.
